landing.title: Reduce the risk attackers create through people.
landing.body: MARICS helps organizations understand and reduce human cybersecurity risk through realistic scenarios, measurable habits, and explainable training.
landing.intro: Security awareness that behaves like the real world.
landing.introBody: People do not fail security tests because they lack a policy. They face pressure, authority, urgency, and trust in the moment. MARICS makes those moments safe to practice.
landing.how: A clearer path to safer decisions
landing.security: Built with privacy and security at the centre
landing.cta: Turn human risk into a practice you can improve.
landing.footer: MARICS Security. Human resilience, made measurable.

assessment.title: How do you respond under pressure?
assessment.body: Ten short situations help us understand the moments that need your attention. There is no perfect score.

questions.prompt: Your bank texts: Suspicious activity detected. Confirm within 10 minutes. What do you do?
options: Open the link before the account is locked.
Open your banking app directly or call the number on your card.
Reply STOP and wait for another message.

questions.prompt: A senior colleague requests an urgent payment change by email. What is safest?
options: Pay it now because the request is from a senior person.
Reply to the email asking for confirmation.
Verify using a known phone number or another trusted channel.

questions.prompt: A courier message includes a small fee and a shortened link. What is safest?
options: Use the courier's official website or app to check the delivery.
Click the link but do not enter your card details.
Forward it to a friend to see whether it looks real.

questions.prompt: A caller says your identity will be reported unless you confirm your details immediately. What do you do?
options: Share enough details to prove who you are.
End the call and contact the organization through an official number.
Ask the caller to call back later.

questions.prompt: A familiar contact sends a new bank account number from an unusual address. What is safest?
options: Use the new details because you recognize the name.
Ask them to resend the email.
Verify the change through a separate trusted channel.

questions.prompt: A software offer says only one license remains and payment must happen now. What do you do?
options: Pay quickly before the offer disappears.
Check the vendor through its official website and procurement process.
Share the offer with coworkers and let them decide.

questions.prompt: A group chat mocks you for not opening a shared document. What is safest?
options: Open it so you do not hold up the group.
Ask who created it and verify the link before opening.
Download it on your phone instead.

questions.prompt: A marketplace seller asks for payment outside the platform to save a fee. What do you do?
options: Keep payment and communication on the platform.
Pay half now and the rest on delivery.
Send your banking details so they can invoice you.

questions.prompt: A login page asks you to enter your password again after arriving from an unexpected message. What is safest?
options: Enter it if the logo looks correct.
Navigate to the service directly and sign in there.
Use the same password only once.

questions.prompt: A message appears to come from your manager asking for confidential staff data. What do you do?
options: Send it because the request is internal.
Reply and ask why they need it.
Verify the request through a trusted channel and follow data-sharing policy.
